q: The second-order term in optimal channel coding (normal approximation) at rate R below capacity C is characterised by the channel dispersion V. The probability of error at block length n is approximately:
opts: Q((C−R)√(n/V)) where Q is the Q-function (tail of the standard normal)
exp: Polyanskiy-Poor-Verdú (2010): the optimal rate at block length n and error ε satisfies R* ≈ C − √(V/n)·Q⁻¹(ε) + O(log n / n), where V = E[(log P(Y|X)/P(Y))²] − C² is the channel dispersion. The Q-function correction gives the √n second-order term.
